goal: Phase 1 (launch-and-refusals) of campaign chain-ergonomics-and-fairness: a run launched with --base-ref validates against that ref so a chained contract reading the previous phase's files launches without the operator touching the checkout, and every refusal on the campaign path names the way forward. Spec: docs/campaigns/chain-ergonomics-and-fairness/spec/SPEC.md.

definitionOfDone.text: base-ref, chain and cli tests pass
npm run docs:check finds the manual current
a contract reading a file that exists only on the base ref launches with --base-ref and is refused without it, and both the chain and the CLI take the same path

taskPacket.objective: run --base-ref <ref> validates the contract against that ref instead of the working tree, so a contract whose readFiles name files created by the previous phase launches from any checkout; the chain therefore no longer needs the land branch checked out.
instructions: Evidence (measured 2026-09-17, campaign adversarial-planner): supervise campaign validates each manifest entry in a throwaway worktree of the land branch (src/campaign/chain.mjs validateManifestEntryAtLaunch -> validateContractAgainstRef) and then launches `run --base-ref <land branch>`; src/cli.mjs's run path calls validateContract(...) against the checkout before setLaunchBaseRef, so contract 1d (reading src/cli/plan.mjs, created by the previous phase) failed with 'detached bootstrap failed before readiness' and the campaign parked with launch_failed. The operator's workaround was `git checkout --detach <land branch>`.

Change, src/cli.mjs run path: when --base-ref is given, validate through the same ref-aware path the chain uses (export and reuse validateContractAgainstRef from src/campaign/chain.mjs, or move that helper to a module both can import if the import direction is wrong -- cli may import campaign, campaign must not import cli). Keep assertLaunchBaseClean and everything else in order; without --base-ref nothing changes. Warnings and reusedDoneWarnings still print.

Tests, test/repo/base-ref.test.mjs: 'run --base-ref validates against the ref' builds a temp repo whose HEAD lacks a file that exists on the base ref, writes a contract whose readFiles name it, and asserts the launch succeeds with --base-ref and fails without it (the failure message names the missing file).
Docs: docs/COMMANDS.md's authored prose for `## faberun run` gains one sentence on what --base-ref validates against, then `npm run docs`.
decisions: One validation path for a launch that declares a base; the chain and the CLI stop disagreeing about what a contract is validated against.
nonGoals: No change to what the chain does after a successful launch.

taskPacket.objective: Two refusals on the campaign path say what to do next: campaign unpark refusing a still-parked run names --force, and the promotion refusing a land branch that is checked out says to detach the checkout.
instructions: Evidence (measured 2026-09-17): `faberun campaign unpark <id>` printed 'run <id> is still parked; resume it first or pass --force' -- it does name --force, so check the current text first and only change it if it does not; and the coordinator printed 'refusing to promote campaign/<id>: it is checked out in <repo>' with no hint that detaching the checkout is the fix, which cost the operator a cycle. Read src/campaign/unpark.mjs and the promotion refusal in src/repo/integrate.mjs before writing.

Change: the promotion refusal message names the remedy ('detach the checkout or run the coordinator from a worktree'); the unpark refusal keeps or gains the same shape. Messages only: no behaviour changes, no new flags.
Tests: test/campaign/unpark.test.mjs and test/repo/integration.test.mjs assert the messages name the remedy; keep the existing assertions on the refusal codes.
decisions: A refusal that names the remedy is the whole change; no behaviour moves.
nonGoals: No new flag, no change to when a refusal happens.
